title: A bump allocator
description:
Hand out memory from one big block by moving a pointer forward.

```
arena of 64 bytes
alloc 10 (align 1) at offset 0
alloc 8 (align 8) at offset 16
alloc 64: out of memory
reset: 0 bytes used
```
hints: `std::size_t start{(m_used + align - 1) / align * align};` rounds up (lesson 6.02).
Print offsets by subtracting `m_buffer.get()` from the returned pointer.
requirements: `class Arena(std::size_t size)` with `void* allocate(std::size_t bytes, std::size_t align)` and `reset()`.
Round the offset up to the alignment; return `nullptr` when it does not fit.
No `free` of single blocks: everything goes at `reset`.
stretch: Add `mark()` and `rewind(mark)` to free everything allocated after a point.
